headline: Clergy who opted out of Social Security and Medicare taxes get a one-time window to opt back in.
what_it_does: Some ministers, members of religious orders, and Christian Science practitioners got an IRS exemption from Social Security and Medicare taxes on their church earnings, which also meant giving up those benefits. Until now that choice could not be undone. This law lets them cancel the exemption by filing with the IRS by their tax return due date for 2030 (usually April 15, 2031), with the change starting in tax year 2029 or 2030. Canceling is permanent, and the IRS must make a plan to tell clergy about this option.

who_it_affects.group: Ministers, members of religious orders, and Christian Science practitioners with a current exemption
who_it_affects.how: They can choose to start paying Social Security and Medicare taxes on their ministry earnings again and earn credits toward benefits, but the choice cannot be reversed.
They will generally still need 10 years of covered work (40 credits) to qualify for Social Security and Medicare benefits.
It must process revocation requests and create a plan to inform eligible clergy about the new option.

when_it_takes_effect: Revocations can take effect for tax year 2029 or 2030; applications are due by the tax filing deadline for tax year 2030 (generally April 15, 2031, or later with an extension).
